items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Kenny Clarke who had been working in the orchestra of Tony Proto... formed an orchestra, and I joined it.

ctx.x: We got out of the car on the left side and Burton got it back on the road. Everybody was really worried now. Ram was sitting in the front seat with Burton, Buster on the left side, George in the middle and me on the right. We were rolling along at a fast twenty miles again and suddenly we felt the car jumping as though all four tires had gone flat. I sat up to see what was happening and saw that we were on a rail road track. We were actually going along on the track. George and I looked back at the same time and…

Jack McVey was a tenor sax man in San Francisco who was very well known on the West Coast. He had a band in a place called Jack's tavern and for his first anniversary there, the owner celebrated with a turkey dinner and cocktails starting at two p.m. The John Kirby orchestra was invited and it was really a ball. A jam session was really the order of the afternoon and McVey started it rolling with Cappy Oliver on trumpet, Chuck Bailey, Raborn Tarrant, and Frank Clarke, the bass playing brother of Kenny Clarke.…

Our next move came a couple of weeks after we finished at Burton's lounge. We were engaged to play in San Diego at a place called the Silver Slipper. We left San Francisco on a train that carried no heavy baggage and only went to Bakersfield from where we took a bus to arrive in San Diego. The trip was beautiful and we were in San Diego early in the afternoon. We went to the Silver Slipper which was in the down town section of the city but the club was a run down joint. We had to wait there until our baggage…

items.q: I rang Mickey Baker, guitarist, Kenny Clark, drummer, Art Simmons, piano, Benny Water, sax-tenor, Cecily Forde, singer and some others. We did the show

ctx.x: I went back to play at the Trois Mailletz. I had been angry for some time with Madame Calvé, but decided to forget the difference. Past was past, and it's nice sometimes to play in a club. Another club where I started to play was the Caveau de la Huchette, also situated in the Latin Quarter, which had been bought by Danny Doris, the vibraphonist with whom I had worked quite a few times. The atmosphere of the Huchette was more easier going than at the Trois Mailletz, where people came more to listen to music. In…

A famous well known French composer and singer, Guy Béart, contacted me. He had a T.V. programme called "Bienvenue" which means "Welcome" to Guy Béart. He wss having that programme about twice a month, andhe was inviting all kinds of personalities for his show. He told me that he wanted to make a show called "Bienvenue to American artists", and asked me if I was willing to contact the American musicians available in Paris. I rang Mickey Baker, guitarist, Kenny Clark, drummer, Art Simmons, piano, Benny Water,…

We were all very excited to be with Duke. He came on the T.V. set at 5 p.m., dressed in a light blue costume(it was in July). Guy Béart introduced him to the audience, because Guy Béart always had his emission semi-public with personalities, artists, guests, press, and a lot of beautiful girls, who were engaged especially to add more class to the show.
